title: Use running source node (node-1)
narration: The source node is already running at http://localhost:3001 and is pre-authenticated. We will skip cold-start and login and proceed to verify the UI is ready.
expectedEvidence: Source node responds and the composer is visible.

title: Authenticate to TracoHub on node 1
narration: Connect to the running source node at http://localhost:3001 and authenticate so the demo runs inside a user session instead of an anonymous browser shell.
expectedEvidence: The composer and user navigation controls are visible on the source node.

title: Create a project and switch selection
narration: Create a new project and keep it selected so the next chat becomes part of the shared handoff context.
expectedEvidence: A project is visible in the sidebar with the active state.

title: Create a new chat under the project
narration: Open a fresh chat while the project is selected so the conversation inherits the project scoped context.
expectedEvidence: A blank chat route is open with the composer focused.

title: Prompt in the chat
narration: Send the first prompt that sets up the handoff candidate and creates the source chat we will publish and transfer.
expectedEvidence: The chat route contains a persistent chat identifier and the user message is stored.

title: Publish the project and the chat
narration: Publish the project snapshot and then publish the active chat snapshot so the second node can discover and pull the same working context.
expectedEvidence: Active project and chat share identifiers exist in the source node APIs.

title: Use running target node (node-2)
narration: The target node is already running at http://localhost:3000 and is pre-authenticated. We will skip cold-start and login; verify the node is reachable and ready to pull the published project.
expectedEvidence: Target node responds and the pull project control is visible.

title: Pull the published project and chat on node 2
narration: On the running target node at http://localhost:3000 (already authenticated), pull the remote project through the sidebar, switch into the pulled project, and then pull the published chat snapshot into that local workspace.
expectedEvidence: The pulled project is visible on node 2 and the pulled chat opens with the source message history.

title: Use at mention discovery from node 1
narration: Back on node one, type the at symbol to discover remote agents from node two, then select the reviewer route so the next prompt targets that remote node.
expectedEvidence: The route selector shows the remote reviewer from node 2.

title: Prompt the remote agent to handoff at node 1
narration: Send the remote reviewer prompt from node one so the system creates a pending handoff session instead of continuing locally.
expectedEvidence: Node 1 shows a queued handoff confirmation message.

title: Accept the handoff at node 2
narration: On the running target node at http://localhost:3000, open the handoff inbox, inspect the pending request, and accept it so the remote node can continue from the transferred prompt.
expectedEvidence: The inbox item changes to accepted.

title: Verify the handoff outcome
narration: Finish by verifying that the source session reflects the accepted state, proving that the remote handoff completed across the two isolated nodes.
expectedEvidence: The handoff session status is accepted on the source node.
